details.value: Apex of arytenoid cartilage (continuation of oblique arytenoid fibers)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Lateral margin of epiglottis, running within the aryepiglottic fold

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Recurrent laryngeal nerve (CN X)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior and inferior thyroid arteries

details.label: Action
details.value: Closes the laryngeal inlet (vestibule) during deglutition; airway protection

details.label: Relations
details.value: Aryepiglottic fold contains the cuneiform cartilage and ends at the corniculate cartilage; piriform recess lies lateral to it (foreign bodies lodge here; internal laryngeal nerve runs beneath its mucosa)

pearl: Supraglottic cancer and epiglottitis both involve the aryepiglottic folds. Adult with sore throat, muffled 'hot potato' voice, drooling and stridor: thumb-sign epiglottis with thickened aryepiglottic folds on lateral neck X-ray means impending airway loss; secure the airway first. Supraglottic tumors metastasize to nodes early (rich lymphatics), unlike glottic tumors.

name: Thyroepiglottic muscle (thyroepiglottic part of thyroarytenoid)
function: Upper slip of the thyroarytenoid that runs to the epiglottis and widens the laryngeal inlet, opposing the aryepiglottic sphincter action.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Inner surface of thyroid cartilage lamina (superior fibers of thyroarytenoid)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Lateral margin of epiglottis and aryepiglottic fold

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Recurrent laryngeal nerve (CN X)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior and inferior thyroid arteries

details.label: Action
details.value: Widens the laryngeal inlet by acting on the aryepiglottic folds (Gray's/Snell: the inlet's dilator, antagonist of the aryepiglottic/oblique arytenoid sphincter). Its effect on the epiglottis itself is contested: a minority of sources describe slight epiglottic lowering or inlet closure during swallowing, so do not learn it as an epiglottic depressor.

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies in the quadrangular membrane region lateral to the laryngeal vestibule

pearl: All intrinsic laryngeal muscles except cricothyroid are RLN territory; the left RLN loops under the aortic arch, so left vocal cord palsy can herald lung cancer or an enlarged left atrium (Ortner syndrome).

name: Sphincter pupillae
function: Circular smooth muscle of the iris; parasympathetic contraction constricts the pupil (miosis) in the light and near reflexes, limiting light entry and improving depth of focus.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Circular smooth-muscle fibers (neuroectoderm-derived, from the optic cup; not neural crest) within the iris stroma near the pupillary margin

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Encircles the pupillary margin as a continuous ring

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Parasympathetic: Edinger-Westphal nucleus -> CN III -> ciliary ganglion -> short ciliary nerves (M3 receptors)

details.label: Action
details.value: Miosis; efferent limb of the pupillary light reflex and the near (accommodation) triad

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Major arterial circle of the iris (long posterior and anterior ciliary arteries)

pearl: Compressive CN III palsy (PCOM aneurysm, uncal herniation) hits superficial parasympathetic fibers first: fixed dilated pupil. Pilocarpine constricts it; tropicamide/atropine block it.

name: Dilator pupillae
function: Radial smooth muscle of the iris; sympathetic contraction widens the pupil (mydriasis) in dim light and with arousal, increasing light entry to the retina.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Radial myoepithelial fibers arising from the iris root at the ciliary margin

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Runs toward the pupillary margin, posterior/deep to the sphincter pupillae

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Sympathetic: hypothalamus -> T1 -> superior cervical ganglion -> carotid plexus -> long ciliary nerves (alpha-1 receptors)

details.label: Action
details.value: Mydriasis; dilated pupil of the fight-or-flight response and dim-light vision

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Major arterial circle of the iris

pearl: Horner syndrome: ptosis, miosis, anhidrosis. Cocaine fails to dilate; hydroxyamphetamine dilates only if lesion is pre-ganglionic; apraclonidine reverses anisocoria (denervation supersensitivity).

name: Ciliary muscle
function: Smooth muscle ring in the ciliary body; parasympathetic contraction relaxes zonular fibers so the lens rounds up for near vision, and opens the trabecular meshwork to aid aqueous outflow.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Scleral spur (anterior sclera at the corneoscleral junction)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Ciliary body stroma and choroid; longitudinal (Brucke), radial and circular (Muller) fiber groups

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Parasympathetic: CN III (Edinger-Westphal) via ciliary ganglion and short ciliary nerves (M3 receptors)

details.label: Action
details.value: Accommodation for near vision; longitudinal fibers pull on the scleral spur, opening the trabecular meshwork to increase aqueous outflow

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Anterior and long posterior ciliary arteries (major arterial circle)

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Meridional (longitudinal) fibers (outer; scleral spur to choroid, open the trabecular meshwork); circular fibers (inner sphincter ring; slacken the zonular fibers for accommodation)

pearl: Pilocarpine contracts it to open the trabecular meshwork (open-angle glaucoma); in acute angle closure it works mainly via miosis pulling the iris off the angle. Cycloplegics (atropine, cyclopentolate) paralyze it: blurred near vision. Presbyopia is lens stiffening, not muscle weakness; CN III palsy adds loss of accommodation.

name: Depressor septi nasi
function: Small muscle of the upper lip and nose that pulls the nasal septum and tip downward and narrows the nostril; active in sniffing and during a broad smile.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Incisive fossa of the maxilla

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Nasal septum and posterior part of the ala of the nose

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Zygomatic and buccal branches of the facial nerve (CN VII)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior labial artery of the facial artery

details.label: Action
details.value: Narrows the nostril and draws the septum downward

pearl: Overactivity drops the nasal tip and shortens the upper lip when smiling, a target for rhinoplasty; in Bell palsy it is paralysed with the rest of the mid-face muscles, so the nostril on that side no longer flares with inspiration.

name: Vocalis
function: Medial bundle of the thyroarytenoid lying beside the vocal ligament; it fine-tunes pitch by tensing the anterior part and relaxing the posterior part of the vocal ligament, so segments of the fold can vibrate differently.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Vocal process of the arytenoid cartilage

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Vocal ligament (and the angle of the thyroid cartilage along with it)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Recurrent laryngeal nerve (CN X)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior and inferior thyroid arteries

details.label: Action
details.value: Tenses the anterior vocal ligament and relaxes the posterior vocal ligament for fine control of pitch and vocal quality

details.label: Relations
details.value: Forms the body of the vocal fold under the lamina propria and epithelium; lateral to it the main thyroarytenoid and the conus elasticus below

pearl: The vocal fold has a soft cover (epithelium and superficial lamina propria, Reinke space) over the stiff vocalis body; nodules, polyps and Reinke oedema (smokers) sit in the cover. Recurrent laryngeal palsy leaves the fold in the paramedian position with a breathy voice.

name: Subclavius
function: Small muscle under the clavicle running from the first rib to the middle third of the clavicle; it anchors and depresses the clavicle and cushions the subclavian vessels and brachial plexus beneath a fractured clavicle.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Upper border of the first rib and its costal cartilage

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Inferior surface of the middle third of the clavicle (subclavian groove)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Nerve to subclavius (C5–C6, from the upper trunk of the brachial plexus)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Clavicular branch of the thoracoacromial artery

details.label: Action
details.value: Anchors and depresses the clavicle, steadying it during shoulder movement

details.label: Relations
details.value: Subclavian vein lies directly below and behind it, then the subclavian artery and trunks of the brachial plexus; the costoclavicular ligament is medial

pearl: In a midshaft clavicle fracture the subclavius pads the subclavian vein and artery against the sharp fragments, so neurovascular injury is uncommon. Its hypertrophy or a cervical rib narrows the costoclavicular space (thoracic outlet syndrome); it lies in the path of subclavian vein cannulation.

name: Frontal belly of occipitofrontalis (frontalis)
function: Anterior belly of the scalp muscle; it has no bony attachment and raises the eyebrows and wrinkles the forehead horizontally.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Epicranial aponeurosis at the level of the coronal suture

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Skin of the frontal region and eyebrows (blending with procerus, corrugator supercilii and orbicularis oculi)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Temporal branches of CN VII

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Frontal branch of superficial temporal artery (with supraorbital and supratrochlear arteries)

details.label: Action
details.value: Raises the eyebrows and wrinkles the skin of the forehead horizontally

pearl: Forehead sparing marks an upper motor neuron facial palsy, because the part of the facial nucleus supplying frontalis receives bilateral cortical input; in Bell palsy the forehead cannot wrinkle.

name: Occipital belly of occipitofrontalis (occipitalis)
function: Posterior belly of the scalp muscle; it pulls the scalp backward and anchors the epicranial aponeurosis so the frontal belly can lift the brows.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Lateral two-thirds of the superior nuchal line and the mastoid process

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Epicranial aponeurosis and skin of the occipital region

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Posterior auricular nerve (branch of CN VII)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Occipital branch of posterior auricular artery and descending branch of occipital artery

details.label: Action
details.value: Moves the scalp backward and fixes the epicranial aponeurosis

pearl: The posterior auricular nerve leaves CN VII just below the stylomastoid foramen, so the occipital belly is spared by lesions of the facial nerve within the parotid gland.

name: Epicranial aponeurosis (galea aponeurotica)
function: Tough tendinous sheet over the calvaria that joins the frontal and occipital bellies of occipitofrontalis and forms the third layer of the scalp.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Occipital bellies of occipitofrontalis posteriorly; superior nuchal line and external occipital protuberance between them

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Frontal bellies of occipitofrontalis anteriorly; continuous laterally with the temporal fascia, where auricularis anterior and superior arise

details.label: Innervation
details.value: None of its own (its muscle bellies are supplied by CN VII)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Scalp arteries run in the dense connective tissue superficial to it

details.label: Action
details.value: Transmits the pull of the frontal and occipital bellies; moves with the skin as one unit over the loose areolar layer

pearl: A scalp wound that divides the aponeurosis coronally gapes widely because the two bellies pull the edges apart; the loose areolar layer beneath it is the danger area, through which blood and infection spread to the eyelids and via emissary veins to the cranial cavity.

name: Orbital part of orbicularis oculi
function: Thick outer ring of the eyelid sphincter that surrounds the orbital margin and screws the eyes tightly shut.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Medial orbital margin (nasal part of frontal bone, frontal process of maxilla) and medial palpebral ligament

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Fibers loop around the orbit without interruption and return to the medial palpebral ligament; skin around the orbit

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Temporal and zygomatic branches of CN VII

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Facial and superficial temporal arteries

details.label: Action
details.value: Forceful (voluntary) closure of the eyelids; draws the brow and cheek skin toward the eye

pearl: Squeezing the eyes shut against resistance tests it; its contraction produces the lateral 'crow's feet' wrinkles treated with botulinum toxin.

name: Palpebral part of orbicularis oculi
function: Thin inner part of the eyelid sphincter lying within the lids in front of the orbital septum and tarsi; closes the lids gently in blinking and sleep.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Medial palpebral ligament

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Lateral palpebral ligament (raphe), arching across both eyelids anterior to the tarsi

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Zygomatic (and temporal) branches of CN VII

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Facial and superficial temporal arteries

details.label: Action
details.value: Gentle and reflex closure of the eyelids (blink); spreads the tear film and holds the lower lid against the globe

pearl: Paralysis in CN VII palsy causes lagophthalmos with exposure keratitis, and the unsupported lower lid falls away from the globe (paralytic ectropion) so tears spill over (epiphora).

name: Superficial part of masseter
function: Larger, anterior part of masseter whose fibers slope downward and backward; it elevates the mandible and helps protrude it.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Zygomatic arch: maxillary process of the zygomatic bone and anterior two-thirds of the lower border of the arch

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Angle and lower lateral surface of the ramus of the mandible

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Masseteric nerve (CN V3, anterior division)

details.label: Action
details.value: Elevates and protrudes the mandible

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Transverse facial artery; masseteric branch of maxillary artery and branches of facial artery

pearl: Palpated over the angle of the mandible during jaw clenching to test the motor root of CN V; the parotid duct crosses its surface and turns medially at its anterior border.

name: Deep part of masseter
function: Smaller, posterior part of masseter with vertical fibers hidden by the superficial part; it elevates the mandible and its fibers retract it.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Zygomatic arch: medial surface and posterior third of the lower border

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Upper lateral surface of the ramus and the coronoid process of the mandible

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Masseteric nerve (CN V3, anterior division), entering its deep surface through the mandibular notch

details.label: Action
details.value: Elevates the mandible; deep fibers retract it

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Masseteric branch of maxillary artery; transverse facial artery

pearl: The masseteric nerve and artery reach the muscle through the mandibular notch on its deep surface, so the superficial surface can be dissected without denervating it.

name: Superior head of lateral pterygoid
function: Smaller upper head of lateral pterygoid; it attaches to the capsule and articular disc of the temporomandibular joint and controls the disc as the jaw closes.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Infratemporal surface (and crest) of the greater wing of the sphenoid bone

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Capsule and articular disc of the temporomandibular joint, and the pterygoid fovea

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Mandibular nerve (CN V3), nerve to lateral pterygoid

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Muscular (pterygoid) branches of maxillary artery

details.label: Action
details.value: Draws the articular disc forward with the condyle in protrusion and steadies the disc as it returns during closing

pearl: Spasm or incoordination of this head is implicated in anterior disc displacement, producing the click of temporomandibular joint dysfunction.

name: Inferior head of lateral pterygoid
function: Larger lower head of lateral pterygoid; it pulls the condyle forward onto the articular tubercle to protrude the mandible and open the mouth.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Lateral surface of the lateral pterygoid plate

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Pterygoid fovea on the neck of the condylar process of the mandible

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Mandibular nerve (CN V3), nerve to lateral pterygoid

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Muscular (pterygoid) branches of maxillary artery

details.label: Action
details.value: Bilaterally protrudes the mandible and opens the mouth; unilaterally swings the jaw to the opposite side for grinding

pearl: With a unilateral CN V3 lesion the jaw deviates toward the paralyzed side on opening, pushed across by the intact opposite muscle; the buccal nerve emerges between the two heads and the maxillary artery usually passes between or superficial to them.

name: Anterior belly of digastric
function: First pharyngeal arch belly of digastric in the floor of the mouth; with the mylohyoid it depresses the mandible and raises the hyoid, and it separates the submental from the submandibular triangle.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Digastric fossa of the mandible

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Intermediate tendon, slung to the body of the hyoid bone

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Nerve to mylohyoid (from the inferior alveolar nerve, CN V3)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Branches of the submental artery

details.label: Action
details.value: Raises the hyoid bone and base of the tongue; opens the mouth by lowering the mandible when the hyoid is fixed

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies on mylohyoid; the two anterior bellies and the hyoid bound the submental triangle; forms the anterior boundary of the submandibular triangle

pearl: The two bellies have different nerves because of different arch origins: anterior belly from the 1st arch (CN V3 via nerve to mylohyoid), posterior belly from the 2nd arch (CN VII).

name: Posterior belly of digastric
function: Second pharyngeal arch belly of digastric running from the mastoid to the hyoid; it elevates and retracts the hyoid and is the key surgical landmark of the upper neck.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Mastoid notch of the temporal bone

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Intermediate tendon, slung to the body of the hyoid bone (it pierces the stylohyoid tendon)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Facial nerve (digastric branch, given off just below the stylomastoid foramen)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Muscular branches of the posterior auricular and occipital arteries

details.label: Action
details.value: Elevates and steadies the hyoid bone during swallowing; assists in opening the mouth

details.label: Relations
details.value: Crosses superficial to the internal jugular vein, internal and external carotid arteries, and CN X, XI and XII; forms the posterior boundary of the submandibular triangle and the upper boundary of the carotid triangle

pearl: Surgeons call it the 'resident's friend': everything important in the upper neck (internal jugular vein, carotids, CN X, XI, XII) lies deep to it, and in parotid surgery the facial nerve trunk is found just above its upper border.

name: Straight part of cricothyroid
function: Anterior, nearly vertical part of cricothyroid; it pulls the thyroid cartilage down toward the cricoid arch, tilting it forward to lengthen and tense the vocal ligaments.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Anterolateral surface of the arch of the cricoid cartilage

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Inferior border of the lamina of the thyroid cartilage

details.label: Innervation
details.value: External branch of the superior laryngeal nerve (CN X)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior and inferior thyroid arteries (cricothyroid branch of superior thyroid)

details.label: Action
details.value: Tilts the thyroid cartilage forward and down at the cricothyroid joints, lengthening and tensing the vocal ligaments (raises pitch)

details.label: Relations
details.value: The two straight parts flank the median cricothyroid ligament, the site of emergency cricothyrotomy

pearl: External laryngeal nerve injury during ligation of the superior thyroid artery paralyzes cricothyroid: a weak, easily fatigued voice that cannot reach high pitch.

name: Oblique part of cricothyroid
function: Posterior part of cricothyroid whose fibers run backward to the inferior horn; it draws the thyroid cartilage forward on the cricoid, lengthening and tensing the vocal ligaments.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Anterolateral surface of the arch of the cricoid cartilage (behind the straight part)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Inferior horn of the thyroid cartilage and adjacent lower border of the lamina

details.label: Innervation
details.value: External branch of the superior laryngeal nerve (CN X)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior and inferior thyroid arteries

details.label: Action
details.value: Glides the thyroid cartilage forward on the cricoid at the cricothyroid joints, lengthening and tensing the vocal ligaments

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies just in front of the cricothyroid joint, behind which the recurrent laryngeal nerve enters the larynx; overlapped by sternothyroid

name: Transverse arytenoid
function: The only unpaired intrinsic laryngeal muscle; it bridges the two arytenoid cartilages and pulls them together to close the posterior, intercartilaginous part of the rima glottidis.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Posterior surface and lateral border of one arytenoid cartilage

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Corresponding surface of the opposite arytenoid cartilage

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Recurrent laryngeal nerve (both sides)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior and inferior thyroid arteries (laryngeal branches)

details.label: Action
details.value: Adducts the arytenoid cartilages, closing the intercartilaginous portion of the rima glottidis

details.label: Relations
details.value: Deep to the oblique arytenoids; covered posteriorly by the mucosa of the laryngopharynx

pearl: Because it is a single midline muscle supplied from both sides, it keeps working after a unilateral recurrent laryngeal nerve lesion.

name: Oblique arytenoid
function: Paired bundles that cross like an X on the back of the transverse arytenoid; they adduct the arytenoids and continue into the aryepiglottic folds as the sphincter of the laryngeal inlet.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Muscular process (posterior surface) of one arytenoid cartilage

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Apex of the opposite arytenoid cartilage; some fibers continue as the aryepiglottic part to the epiglottis

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Recurrent laryngeal nerve

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Superior and inferior thyroid arteries (laryngeal branches)

details.label: Action
details.value: Adducts the arytenoid cartilages, closing the intercartilaginous part of the rima glottidis; with the aryepiglottic part narrows the laryngeal inlet

details.label: Relations
details.value: Superficial (posterior) to the transverse arytenoid

name: Cricopharyngeus (cricopharyngeal part of inferior pharyngeal constrictor)
function: Lowest, horizontal part of the inferior constrictor that loops around the pharyngoesophageal junction as the upper esophageal sphincter; tonically closed and relaxing only as the bolus arrives.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Side of the cricoid cartilage

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Encircles the pharyngoesophageal junction to the opposite side of the cricoid without a raphe; blends below with the circular esophageal muscle

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Vagus nerve via the pharyngeal plexus, with branches from the recurrent laryngeal nerve

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Ascending pharyngeal artery and branches of the superior thyroid artery (with the inferior thyroid artery)

details.label: Action
details.value: Upper esophageal sphincter: tonically contracted between swallows to keep air out of the esophagus and prevent reflux; relaxes during swallowing

details.label: Gaps
details.value: Above it, between its fibers and the thyropharyngeal part: Killian dehiscence. Below it: the V-shaped area (of Laimer) of sparse longitudinal esophageal muscle. The recurrent laryngeal nerve passes deep to its lower border

pearl: Failure of cricopharyngeal relaxation raises hypopharyngeal pressure and pushes mucosa out through Killian dehiscence (Zenker diverticulum); it is also the narrowest part of the gut tube, where swallowed foreign bodies lodge and endoscopes perforate.

name: Superior longitudinal muscle of tongue
function: Intrinsic tongue muscle running the length of the dorsum just under the mucosa; shortens the tongue and curls its tip and edges upward.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Submucous fibers at the back of the tongue

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Apex of the tongue; unites with the muscle of the opposite side

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)

details.label: Action
details.value: Shortens the tongue and turns the tip and sides upward

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Deep lingual branch of lingual artery; branches from facial artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Thin sheet immediately beneath the mucosa of the dorsum

name: Inferior longitudinal muscle of tongue
function: Intrinsic tongue muscle running along the under surface; shortens the tongue and curls its tip downward.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Under surface of the tongue between genioglossus and hyoglossus

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Apex of the tongue, blending with styloglossus

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)

details.label: Action
details.value: Shortens the tongue and turns the tip and sides downward

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Deep lingual branch of lingual artery; branches from facial artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Narrow band close to the inferior surface, lateral to genioglossus and medial to hyoglossus; the deep lingual artery runs along it

name: Transverse muscle of tongue
function: Intrinsic tongue muscle running from the midline septum to the lateral margins; narrows and lengthens the tongue.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Median fibrous septum of the tongue

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Dorsum and sides of the tongue

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)

details.label: Action
details.value: Narrows and elongates the tongue (with the vertical muscle, protrudes it)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Deep lingual branch of lingual artery; branches from facial artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Fibers interweave with the vertical muscle between the superior and inferior longitudinal muscles

name: Vertical muscle of tongue
function: Intrinsic tongue muscle running from the dorsum to the under surface at the borders of the forepart; flattens and widens the tongue.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Mucous membrane on the dorsum of the forepart of the tongue

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Fibers extend from the dorsum to the undersurface of the tongue

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)

details.label: Action
details.value: Flattens and broadens the tongue

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Deep lingual branch of lingual artery; branches from facial artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Confined to the borders of the forepart of the tongue; interweaves with the transverse muscle

name: Rectus capitis posterior major
function: Larger of the two posterior recti; extends the head and rotates it to the same side, and forms the superomedial side of the suboccipital triangle.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Spinous process of the axis (C2)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Lateral part of the inferior nuchal line of the occipital bone

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Suboccipital nerve (posterior ramus of C1)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Vertebral artery and descending branch of occipital artery

details.label: Action
details.value: Extends the head and rotates it to the same side

details.label: Relations
details.value: Superomedial boundary of the suboccipital triangle; lateral to rectus capitis posterior minor, deep to semispinalis capitis

pearl: The suboccipital triangle it bounds contains the horizontal segment of the vertebral artery and the suboccipital nerve on the posterior arch of the atlas.

name: Rectus capitis posterior minor
function: Small medial suboccipital muscle from the atlas to the occiput; extends the head at the atlanto-occipital joint. It is not a boundary of the suboccipital triangle.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Tubercle of the posterior arch of the atlas (C1)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Medial part of the inferior nuchal line of the occipital bone

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Suboccipital nerve (posterior ramus of C1)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Vertebral artery and descending branch of occipital artery

details.label: Action
details.value: Extends the head

details.label: Relations
details.value: Medial and deep to rectus capitis posterior major; overlies the posterior atlanto-occipital membrane

name: Obliquus capitis superior
function: Suboccipital muscle from the atlas up to the occiput; extends the head and bends it to the same side, and forms the superolateral side of the suboccipital triangle.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Transverse process of the atlas (C1)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Occipital bone between the superior and inferior nuchal lines

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Suboccipital nerve (posterior ramus of C1)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Vertebral artery and descending branch of occipital artery

details.label: Action
details.value: Extends the head and bends it laterally

details.label: Relations
details.value: Superolateral boundary of the suboccipital triangle

name: Obliquus capitis inferior
function: Only suboccipital muscle that does not reach the skull; it runs from the axis to the atlas and rotates the atlas, turning the face to the same side.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Spinous process of the axis (C2)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Transverse process of the atlas (C1)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Suboccipital nerve (posterior ramus of C1)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Vertebral artery and descending branch of occipital artery

details.label: Action
details.value: Rotates the atlas (and head) to turn the face to the same side

details.label: Relations
details.value: Inferior boundary of the suboccipital triangle; the greater occipital nerve (C2) hooks around its lower border and ascends across it

pearl: The greater occipital nerve winds around its inferior border, a landmark for nerve blocks and a site of entrapment in occipital neuralgia.

name: Rectus capitis anterior
function: Short prevertebral muscle from the atlas to the base of the skull, deep to longus capitis; flexes the head at the atlanto-occipital joint.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Anterior surface of the lateral mass of the atlas

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Base (basilar part) of the occipital bone in front of the foramen magnum and occipital condyle

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Anterior rami of C1–C2

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Muscular branches of the vertebral artery; ascending pharyngeal artery

details.label: Action
details.value: Flexes the head (nodding) and stabilizes the atlanto-occipital joint

details.label: Relations
details.value: Deep to the upper part of longus capitis; anterior to the atlanto-occipital joint

name: Rectus capitis lateralis
function: Short muscle from the transverse process of the atlas to the jugular process of the occipital bone; bends the head to the same side.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Upper surface of the transverse process of the atlas

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Inferior surface of the jugular process of the occipital bone

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Anterior rami of C1–C2

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Muscular branches of the vertebral artery, occipital artery and ascending pharyngeal artery

details.label: Action
details.value: Flexes the head laterally to the same side; stabilizes the atlanto-occipital joint

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lies immediately behind the internal jugular vein as it leaves the jugular foramen; the anterior ramus of C1 emerges medial to it

pearl: It lies directly behind the jugular foramen and is detached in far-lateral approaches to expose the jugular bulb.

name: Longissimus cervicis
function: Cervical portion of the longissimus (intermediate) column of erector spinae; extends the neck and bends it to the same side.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Transverse processes of the upper thoracic vertebrae (T1–T5)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C2–C6

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Posterior rami of lower cervical and upper thoracic spinal nerves

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Occipital, deep cervical and vertebral arteries

details.label: Action
details.value: Bilaterally extends the cervical spine; unilaterally bends it to the same side

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lateral to semispinalis cervicis and medial to iliocostalis cervicis; longissimus capitis lies on its medial side; deep to splenius cervicis

name: Spinalis cervicis
function: Thin, inconstant cervical portion of the spinalis (medial) column of erector spinae, running between spinous processes beside the nuchal ligament; extends the neck.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Lower nuchal ligament and spinous processes of C7 (and upper thoracic vertebrae)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Spinous process of the axis (sometimes C3–C4)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Posterior rami of cervical spinal nerves

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Occipital, deep cervical and vertebral arteries

details.label: Action
details.value: Extends the cervical spine

details.label: Relations
details.value: Most medial erector spinae column, alongside the nuchal ligament; often blended with semispinalis cervicis

name: Multifidus (cervical part)
function: Deep transversospinalis fascicles filling the groove beside the cervical spinous processes; they stabilize the cervical segments during movement.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Articular processes of C4–C7

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Spinous processes of the vertebrae above, spanning two to four segments (up to the axis)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Posterior rami of cervical spinal nerves (medial branches)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Occipital, deep cervical and vertebral arteries

details.label: Action
details.value: Stabilizes the cervical spine; assists extension and rotation to the opposite side

details.label: Relations
details.value: Deep to semispinalis cervicis; superficial to the rotatores cervicis

pearl: Multifidus atrophies with fatty infiltration after whiplash injury and in chronic neck pain, visible on MRI.

name: Interspinales cervicis
function: Short paired segmental muscles joining adjacent cervical spinous processes on each side of the interspinous ligament; aid extension of the neck.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Spinous process of a cervical vertebra (C3–T1)

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Spinous process of the adjacent vertebra above (C2–C7)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Posterior rami of cervical spinal nerves

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Occipital, deep cervical and vertebral arteries

details.label: Action
details.value: Aid in extension of the cervical vertebral column; segmental stabilizers

details.label: Relations
details.value: Paired, one on each side of the interspinous ligament between the bifid cervical spinous processes; best developed in the neck

name: Common tendinous ring (of Zinn)
function: Fibrous ring at the apex of the orbit surrounding the optic canal and the medial part of the superior orbital fissure; common origin of the four rectus muscles.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Periosteum of the body and lesser wing of the sphenoid around the optic canal, bridging the medial part of the superior orbital fissure

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Gives origin to the superior, medial, inferior and lateral rectus muscles

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Nerves passing through the ring: optic nerve (CN II), superior and inferior branches of the oculomotor nerve (CN III), nasociliary nerve (CN V1), abducent nerve (CN VI)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Ophthalmic artery passes through the ring with the optic nerve in the optic canal

details.label: Action
details.value: Fixed anchor for the four recti, which form the muscular cone of the orbit

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Structures outside the ring (through the lateral part of the superior orbital fissure): lacrimal nerve, frontal nerve, trochlear nerve (CN IV), superior ophthalmic vein. Levator palpebrae superioris and superior oblique arise above and medial to the ring; inferior oblique arises from the anterior orbital floor

pearl: Orbital apex syndrome: a lesion at the ring causes ophthalmoplegia (CN III, IV, VI), V1 sensory loss and visual loss (CN II); because the recti attach to the optic nerve sheath here, eye movement is painful in optic neuritis.

name: Superior and inferior tarsi (tarsal plates)
function: Dense fibrous plates that stiffen the eyelids, contain the tarsal (meibomian) glands, and receive the lid elevators.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Superior tarsus (larger, about 10 mm high; receives levator palpebrae superioris and the superior tarsal muscle); inferior tarsus (smaller, about 5 mm high; in the lower lid)

details.label: Origin
details.value: Anchored to the orbital margins by the medial and lateral palpebral ligaments; continuous peripherally with the orbital septum

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Levator palpebrae superioris inserts on the anterior surface, and the superior tarsal (Müller's) muscle on the upper edge, of the superior tarsus

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Sensory: V1 branches (upper lid) and infraorbital nerve, V2 (lower lid)

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Palpebral arcades from the medial and lateral palpebral arteries (ophthalmic and lacrimal arteries)

details.label: Action
details.value: Give the lids shape and firmness; tarsal glands open at the lid margin and secrete the lipid layer of the tear film

pearl: A chalazion is a painless granulomatous lump from a blocked tarsal (meibomian) gland within the tarsus, in contrast to the painful stye (hordeolum) of a lash follicle gland at the lid margin.

name: Temporal fascia
function: Strong fascial sheet covering temporalis from the superior temporal line to the zygomatic arch; gives origin to the superficial fibers of the muscle.

details.label: Divisions
details.value: Superficial layer (attaches to the lateral margin of the upper border of the zygomatic arch); deep layer (attaches to the medial margin); a fat pad lies between them above the arch

details.label: Origin
details.value: Superior temporal line of the frontal and parietal bones

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Upper border of the zygomatic arch, after splitting into superficial and deep layers

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Not applicable (overlying skin: auriculotemporal and zygomaticotemporal nerves)

details.label: Action
details.value: Roofs the temporal fossa and gives origin to temporalis; resists the downward pull of masseter on the zygomatic arch

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Middle temporal artery (from superficial temporal artery) pierces it; superficial temporal vessels lie on its surface

pearl: The temporal branch of the facial nerve crosses the zygomatic arch superficial to this fascia, so surgeons elevate flaps deep to its superficial layer to protect the nerve (Gillies approach to a depressed zygomatic arch runs beneath it).

name: Superficial (investing) layer of deep cervical fascia
function: Outermost layer of deep cervical fascia, encircling the whole neck deep to platysma and splitting to enclose sternocleidomastoid and trapezius; it roofs the anterior and posterior triangles.

details.label: Origin
details.value: Above: superior nuchal line, mastoid process, zygomatic arch, lower border of the mandible and hyoid bone; behind: nuchal ligament and cervical spinous processes

details.label: Insertion
details.value: Below: manubrium, clavicle, acromion and spine of scapula; above the manubrium it splits to enclose the suprasternal space (of Burns)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Pierced by the cutaneous branches of the cervical plexus at the posterior border of sternocleidomastoid

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: External and anterior jugular veins run on or pierce it

details.label: Action
details.value: Encloses and compartmentalizes the neck; limits the superficial spread of infection

details.label: Relations
details.value: Splits to enclose sternocleidomastoid and trapezius and the submandibular and parotid glands (parotid and masseteric fascia); the pretracheal layer, carotid sheath and prevertebral layer lie deep to it

pearl: The accessory nerve crosses the posterior triangle just deep to this layer, so it is at risk in lymph node biopsy; the external jugular vein pierces the fascia above the clavicle and is held open there, permitting air embolism if cut.
